summary: For the NASA Space Apps Challenge, we developed an interactive, cooperative space mission simulation game inspired by accessible co-op mechanics. Featuring a Mission Control structure, players receive predefined mission objectives and work together to complete escalating scientific tasks under tight constraints. Our solution directly addresses the challenge of creating a game that allows participants to manage and simulate a complete space mission while navigating complex engineering trade-offs. The game forces players to balance critical real-world resources—such as budget, mass, power, communications, and orbit—as scientific demands progressively increase with each level. Rather than overwhelming users with complex formulas, it translates aerospace engineering into an intuitive, high-engagement team experience. This is important because space mission design is often confined to abstract, theoretical exercises. Our game democratizes STEM education by lowering the entry barrier, allowing students and space enthusiasts to experience authentic engineering constraints hands-on, fostering teamwork, and teaching vital problem-solving skills through immersive gameplay.
details: Our interactive cooperative space mission simulation game operates on a Mission Control structure where players receive assigned objectives and work together to execute escalating scientific tasks under strict constraints. As players advance through progressively harder levels, they must manage critical engineering trade-offs—balancing budget, mass, power, communications, and orbital parameters—to keep the mission successful. The primary benefit and intended impact of this approach is democratizing STEM education by lowering the entry barrier to aerospace engineering, allowing students and enthusiasts to intuitively master complex system dependencies through hands-on experimentation rather than abstract theory. Our creative innovation lies in combining the fast-paced, collaborative mechanics of party management games like Overcooked with authentic NASA mission constraints, turning dry resource balancing into an engaging team challenge. During development, we carefully considered the balance of the game accessibility with scientific validity, structured a gradual learning curve, and scoped modular levels for high replayability. To build the project, our team utilized JavaScript for the coding.
